title: jobban szeretem: Liking One Thing Better

sections.title: Reusing jobban for taste
sections.content: You already know jobban ("better") as the irregular comparative of jól, and you already know szeretem, the definite form of szeret, for liking one specific thing. Put them together — jobban szeretem — and you get "I like it better", the natural way to compare how much you like two named things. Add mint, exactly as before, to say what it beats.

sections.title: Comparing what you like
rows: Jobban szeretem a teát, mint a kávét.
I like tea better than coffee.
Jobban szereted a nyarat, mint a telet?
Do you like summer better than winter?
Ildikó jobban szereti a filmeket, mint a könyveket.
Ildikó likes films better than books.

items.spanish: Jobban szeretem a magyar konyhát, mint az olaszt.
items.english: I like Hungarian cuisine better than Italian.

items.spanish: Károly jobban szereti a hegyeket, mint a tengert.
items.english: Károly likes the mountains better than the sea.

sections.content: jobban szeretem compares two named things you both like to some degree ("tea vs. coffee"), while inkább is about the choice you're making right now ("I'd rather have tea") — often you'll reach for both together in the same conversation.
